lessons.title: What is Git?
lessons.content: Git tracks changes to your files over time, letting you save checkpoints (commits), review history, and collaborate without overwriting each other's work.
lessons.notes: A commit is a snapshot of your staged changes, not the whole project re-copied.
lessons.mistakes: Committing generated files or secrets that should be in .gitignore instead.
lessons.practice: Write out the three commands needed to initialize a repo and make a first commit.
lessons.challenge: Explain in your own words the difference between 'staged' and 'committed'.
lessons.code:
git init
git add .
git commit -m "Initial commit"
lessons.expectedOutput: Creates a new repository with one saved commit.
